extracted.intended_audience: beginner to intermediate GAP users / mathematicians learning the GAP language
extracted.subtask_description: Introductory tutorial material for writing and using functions, lists, sets, ranges, loops, vectors/matrices and records in the GAP programming language. Covers syntax, semantics, mutability/identity, and common library utilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function application syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions are applied by writing the function name followed by arguments in parentheses; several arguments are separated by commas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Factorial(17); Gcd(1234, 5678); functions behave like mathematical functions and return an object or produce a side effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures (functions that produce side effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some functions produce no return value but only side effects (e.g., modify arguments or print); these are sometimes called procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Print(1234, "\n"); prints output and returns no meaningful object. Be aware of side effects when using such functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions that both mutate and return values
rubrics_metrics.description: Some functions change an argument (mutate) and also return an object describing the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Sortex sorts a list in-place and returns the permutation applied. Check function docs for whether a function mutates its arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple anonymous function (maps-to operator ->)
rubrics_metrics.description: A comfortable way to define a simple function is using the maps-to operator ->, e.g., cubed := x -> x^3;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines a function object that can be applied like cubed(5); For more complicated/multi-argument functions see function ... end syntax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function definition form (function ... end)
rubrics_metrics.description: Full function definitions use the syntax function(arguments) statements end and may include local declarations, control flow, and return statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition is an expression and can be assigned to a name (sayhello := function() ... end;). The terminating semicolon belongs to the assignment, not the function syntax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help system query format
rubrics_metrics.description: Help queries follow ?[book:][?]topic with optional book restriction and optional extra ? for substring search; search is case-insensitive and whitespace-normalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ?help, ?tut:sets, ??sets (substring search), ?books lists books. When multiple matches appear, use ?n to select a match.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice for large input
rubrics_metrics.description: For large amounts of input, write input into a file and then read it into GAP using Read or Edit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid entering very long sessions interactively; use files for maintainability and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: List literal syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: A list is a comma-separated collection enclosed in brackets, e.g., [2,3,5,7,...].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists may contain heterogeneous objects, holes, and other lists. Use [] for the empty list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appending and adding elements (Append vs Add)
rubrics_metrics.description: Append(list, another_list) appends the second list to the first and mutates the first; Add(list, element) adds a single element and mutates the list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both functions change the given list in place and return no value. Use them when you intend to mutate; otherwise copy first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and Length
rubrics_metrics.description: Single elements are accessed by position with list[i]; Length(list) returns the last occupied position (list length).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigning to list positions beyond the current end extends the list and may create holes; the list must exist before assigning to positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating holes by indexed assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigning to a far index (e.g., primes[20] := 71) creates holes in the list but is still a valid list with increased Length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holes are allowed; many list operations and properties differ when holes exist (e.g., dense vs non-dense lists).

rubrics_metrics.name: Position function behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Position(list, element) returns the index of the first occurrence of element in list, or the special object fail if not found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Position to find indices; check for 'fail' special object rather than relying on booleans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lists can be nested and self-referential
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists may contain other lists or even themselves as elements; printing uses a tilde (~) to denote the object currently printed to avoid infinite recursion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful with self-referential structures; printing and some operations may show abbreviation symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strings as special dense lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Strings are dense lists of characters. Character literals can be entered with single quotes; string literals with double quotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strings are handled specially by Print; equality between a character list and a string literal holds (e.g., s1 = "Hallo world."); see Strings and Characters reference for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublists using { } operator
rubrics_metrics.description: list{positions} forms a new list whose i-th entry is the element at position positions[i] of the original list; can be used in extraction and assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: sl := lll{[1,2,3]}; sl{[2,3]} := ["New String", false]; The operator builds new lists (not views).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality vs identity for objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Equality (=) compares contents (structural equality). Assignment (:=) makes two variables name the same object (identity), so mutating via one name affects the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that numbers, permutations, booleans have no subobjects and are immutable; copying references for mutable objects requires explicit copy if autonomy is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: ShallowCopy semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: ShallowCopy(object) returns a new mutable object whose top-level container is new but whose entries are the same subobjects (no deep copy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ShallowCopy when you want to mutate top-level structure without duplicating subobjects. If subobjects are mutable, changes may still be shared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immutable semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Immutable(list) returns an immutable copy: (1) the copy and its subobjects cannot be changed; (2) mutable parts have been copied so the immutable copy shares no mutable subobjects with the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempting to assign into an immutable list triggers an error. Immutable is useful to protect generator lists of groups or other internal data from accidental modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutable vs immutable object rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects of types without subobjects (integers, permutations, booleans) are inherently immutable; lists and records may be mutable or immutable depending on construction and functions used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing complex objects, prefer immutable components where invariants must be preserved; use ShallowCopy/Immutable appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set as special sorted dense list
rubrics_metrics.description: A set in GAP is a dense (no holes), strictly sorted list with no duplicates; elements are required to be comparable via <.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IsSSortedList to test; Set(list) constructs a set from a list by removing holes/duplicates and sorting; Set does not modify its argument, it returns a new set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership operator 'in' and performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'in' operator tests membership and returns a boolean. Membership tests are faster on sets because binary search can be used on sorted data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer sets when many membership tests are needed; for occasional membership checks on small lists, plain lists are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: AddSet behavior (mutating set insertion)
rubrics_metrics.description: AddSet(set, element) inserts element into set in sorted position if not already present, mutating the set in place; if element already present no change occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insertion preserves sorted order. Note adding to a set may be more expensive than appending to a list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersection/Union vs IntersectSet/UniteSet
rubrics_metrics.description: Intersection(A,B) and Union(A,B) take (possibly non-set) lists and return a new set representing intersection/union; IntersectSet/UniteSet mutate their first argument to be the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the mutating or non-mutating variant depending on whether you want to preserve or update the original set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range literal and compact representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A range is an arithmetic progression written as [first,second..last] (or [first..last] for step 1). Long ranges print compactly (e.g., [1 .. 999999]) and have compact internal representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IsRange tests for range objects; ConvertToRangeRep converts a list that is a range to its compact internal representation. Mutating an entry can break range representation without changing the abstract list value.

rubrics_metrics.name: For loop general form and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: for var in list do statements od; iterates over each element of list with var bound to each element in turn; a for loop is a statement and returns no value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'for var from first to last' form is a special case where the list is a range. Remember to terminate the loop with od and semicolon when used as statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: While loop syntax and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: while condition do statements od; repeats statements while condition evaluates to true and is terminated by od.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use while for condition-driven loops; ensure termination or provide interruption (Ctl-C) for long-running loops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveats when mutating lists being iterated
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists used as the body of a for-loop may be mutated (e.g., Unbind to delete entries) during iteration; this can be useful (sieve algorithm) but requires care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Using Unbind(numbers[n-1]) inside loops to implement a sieve; altering the iterated list can change which elements are seen next.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product, Sum, List, Filtered, ForAll utilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Higher-level list utilities: Product(list) multiplies elements; Sum(list) sums elements or Sum(list, f) sums f applied to elements; List(list,f) maps f over list; Filtered(list,prop) returns elements satisfying prop; ForAll(list,prop) checks predicate holds for all elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions abstract common loops and are convenient and often more readable than explicit loops; functions passed as properties should return booleans for Filtered/ForAll.

rubrics_metrics.name: Row vectors and matrices representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Row vectors are dense lists of elements from a common field; matrices are dense lists of row vectors of equal length; indexing is m[row][col].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vectors support addition and scalar multiplication; vector*vector gives scalar product. Matrices support multiplication with vectors and matrices; if dimensions mismatch missing entries are treated as zeros (results may be unexpected).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutability rules for arithmetic results
rubrics_metrics.description: Arithmetical operations that result in vectors produce mutable vectors except in the binary-operation case when both operands are immutable, in which case the result may be immutable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the mutability of results from arithmetic to avoid accidental shared-state bugs; if needed, explicitly copy results before mutating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display vs Print for finite field matrices
rubrics_metrics.description: Finite field matrices are nicer to read when Display is used rather than Print; Display formats matrix entries using field primitives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Display( m * One( GF(5) ) ); produces a readable matrix layout with field elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submatrix extraction and assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Submatrices can be extracted using mat{rows}{columns} and assigned to, provided the containing matrix is mutable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: sm := m{[1,2]}{[2,3]}; sm{[1,2]}{[2]} := [[-2],[0]];; Assignment to submatrices requires the big matrix to be mutable (not the result of an arithmetic operation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order computation and potential infinite order warning
rubrics_metrics.description: Order(element) computes the group-theoretic order of an element; for matrices with complex entries the method may not prove infinite order and issue a warning 'order ... might be infinite'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you suspect infinite order you may need to interrupt GAP and apply other methods (e.g., examine minimal polynomial) to prove infinitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record construction and component access
rubrics_metrics.description: Records are built as rec(name := value, ...). Components are accessed via record.component and assignments create or resize components (mutating the record).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: date := rec(day := 14, month := "Jul", year := 1997); date.year returns 1997. Assigning new components (date.time := rec(...)) expands the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: RecNames and checking bound components
rubrics_metrics.description: RecNames(record) returns a list of the names of all bound components of the record as strings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RecNames to inspect which components exist before accessing them to avoid errors from unbound components.
